analysis: The change is limited to SSDPrefixCachePolicy.swift (T-041, TB-007, A-001) plus tests. maxStageBytes and maxStageMillis keep their defaults (1 GiB, 1000 ms). Their parsing moves into private helpers, configuredMaxStageBytes and configuredMaxStageMillis, with the same validation (positive values, overflow guard). New completeCheckpointMaxStageBytes and completeCheckpointMaxStageMillis (head lines 157-177) raise the defaults for complete-checkpoint (CBv2 hybrid) staging to 3 GiB and 2500 ms when physical memory is at least 96 GiB. Explicit environment settings still win, and invalid settings fall back to the memory-based default. Crypto, TTL (still max 30 minutes), HMAC lookup naming, disk budget and the DBK3 AAD are untouched, so the T-041 at-rest posture (a)-(d) is unchanged. The only effect is on posture (e): the transient staging RAM reservation and pre-submit read latency for complete checkpoints grow on large-memory Macs. The 3 GiB + 1 MiB estimate at 1.5 GB/s is about 2148 ms, under the 2500 ms cap, as the new test asserts. A longer pre-engine.submit stage could use more of the coordinator dispatch deadline, a minor availability and TTFT effect. The TTFT-oracle width is not obviously changed, because larger hits only extend which prefixes are restorable (SEC-035 accepted). The test-only change in ModelCheckpointStorageArtifacts.swift line 36 uses the new cap as the read limit for authenticated streaming; it is not production code. The production callers, such as SSDPrefixCache, the engine and the SSDWriteBehind queue cap (max(512 MiB, maxStageBytes + slack)), were not supplied. A later pass should check that complete-checkpoint callers use the new functions consistently. It should also check that the write-queue byte cap and the GlobalKVCacheBudget reservation account for a 3 GiB donation. The read path's maximumPlaintextBytes bound must stay a hard cap against oversized or hostile files. Nothing in the diff shows a concrete regression.
